maria: Kicking off venatrix-embed v1 onboarding. Running multilingual recall@k + clustering smoke. Observed weird recall@1 drop for short Japanese queries when using per-channel int8 quant. Can someone eyeball? :eyes:
aj: which eval set? short queries = <32 tokens?
maria: Yep. Shortseq holdout (short_queries_v2) — English/JA/FR split. Baseline fp16 recall@1 on JA is 0.82. int8 per-channel -> 0.73. int8 per-tensor -> 0.80.
devon: interesting, per-channel regresses more than per-tensor. any cluster shifts?
maria: Yes — UMAP cluster purity for JA cohort shifted; centroid drift on a handful of topic clusters. embedding L2 norm mean dropped by ~0.12.
lena: can you paste the run command and quant config?
maria: run: `python -m evals.run --model venatrix-v1 --quant int8-perchannel --dataset short_queries_v2 --knn hnsw --M 16 --ef_search 128 --batch 512`
maria: quant config excerpt:
```
quant:
  scheme: per_channel
  dtype: int8
  clip: true
  calibrate_batches: 1024
```
aj: did you try int8 with symmetric vs asymmetric? sometimes asymmetric helps on low-norm tails.
maria: tried symmetric only so far. will run asymmetric next.
devon: also check KV cache behavior? not relevant for static embeddings but our transformer norm folding could be different.
lena: what's the top-k recall deltas by language?
maria: summary: EN: fp16 0.89 -> int8-pc 0.88 (small), FR: 0.84 -> 0.82, JA: 0.82 -> 0.73 (big). overall recall@1 delta -0.06.
aj: can you dump a few failing JA queries + nearest neighbors (fp16 vs int8-pc)?
maria: pasted samples to gdrive: https://redwood-gdrive/venatrix/onboard/ja_fail_samples.csv
devon: quick sanity: try re-normalizing embeddings post-quant (L2 norm to 1) before KNN. sometimes quant alters scale.
maria: doing that now. also toggling HNSW ef_search from 128 -> 256 to rule out index retrieval variance.
maria: local run results: re-normalize + ef_search 256 improved JA int8-pc recall@1 to 0.79. looks like scale + index got us most of the gap.
lena: nice. still want to understand centroid shift though. could be row-wise quant error concentrated on certain dims. try per-channel with smaller clip threshold.
aj: also run per-channel but enable bias-correction pass (our quant tool has --bias-correct). for low-norm languages that helps.
maria: queued bias-correct + asymmetric + clip=0.95. ETA ~30m.
eval-bot: full eval queued: job_id=job_2026_03_23_09_12, docs=48k, languages=[en,fr,ja], metrics=[recall@1,recall@5,cluster_purity,mean_norm]
devon: if the bias-correct run fixes it, probably safe to keep per-channel (best size-speed tradeoff). if not, fallback to per-tensor for JA users or add post-normalize in production route.
maria: agree. I'll follow up with a short writeup and recommended config per-region. thanks all. :thumbsup:
